question:
(a) State the important observation made in the Davisson and Germer experiment when electrons were accelerated through $54\,\text{V}$.
(b) Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of these electrons using $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{Å}$ and state the significance of the result.

options.A:
(a) Electrons were absorbed by the nickel crystal at $54\,\text{V}$.
(b) $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{54}\,\text{Å}\approx0.227\,\text{Å}$, proving particle nature.
options.B:
(a) Scattered electron intensity was uniform at all angles.
(b) $\lambda\approx16.7\,\text{Å}$, which is unrelated to crystal spacing.
options.C:
(a) At about $54\,\text{V}$, a strong maximum in scattered-electron intensity was observed at a definite angle, indicating electron diffraction by crystal planes.
(b) $\lambda=\dfrac{12.27}{\sqrt{54}}\,\text{Å}\approx1.67\,\text{Å}$. Its agreement with the diffraction wavelength confirmed the wave nature of electrons.
options.D:
(a) Electron intensity became zero because electrons lost all charge.
(b) $\lambda=\dfrac{54}{12.27}\,\text{Å}\approx4.40\,\text{Å}$, proving electrons have zero momentum.
